sources: Nautilus, 'The Soviets Drilled the Deepest Hole Ever': drilling began May 24, 1970 on the Kola Peninsula; the deepest point reached 40,230 feet (12,262 m); near 22,000 feet cores held plankton microfossils from two dozen species more than 2 billion years old; near 40,000 feet temperatures reached nearly 356 F (180 C), about twice what was predicted; the rock deformed plastically and crept in to pinch the hole shut; Russia halted drilling in 1992; since 2008 it is sealed with a steel cap about 9 inches across; the 'Well to Hell' story aired on TBN in the late 1980s claiming recorded screams; the site is on the Kola Peninsula near Norway, not Siberia; the screams were a sound loop from the 1972 horror film Baron Blood; a Norwegian teacher admitted he planted the winged-figure story to test the producers; https://nautil.us/the-soviets-drilled-the-deepest-hole-ever-1283561

Skeptoid #4307 (Brian Dunning), 'The Well to Hell': TBN ran 'Scientists Discover Hell' in broadcast and print in late 1989, citing the Finnish source Ammennusastia, a small Evangelical Lutheran magazine, which traced to a reader-contribution section of a Finnish daily newspaper; TBN named a 'Dr. Azzacov'; claimed 14.5 km depth and about 1,100 C in Siberia; Norwegian teacher Age Rendalen sent a fake add-on; the audio first appeared in 2002 and is digitally looped and processed; https://skeptoid.com/episodes/4307

NOAA Ocean Exploration, 'How deep is the ocean?': the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,935 m deep, shallower than the 12,262 m borehole; https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/ocean-depth.html

beats.say: This is the deepest hole humans ever drilled. Over twelve kilometers down.
The Kola Superdeep Borehole, in the Soviet Arctic.
Drilling started in 1970. The record came in 1989.
Twelve thousand, two hundred sixty-two meters. Deeper than the ocean's deepest point.
And the hole is only about nine inches wide.
Nearly seven kilometers down, they found plankton fossils over two billion years old.
